title: What Is League of Legends? The Ultimate Beginner's Guide
description: Discover what League of Legends is, its fascinating history, core gameplay mechanics, and why this iconic multiplayer game captivates millions.

sections.heading: What Is League of Legends?
paragraphs: League of Legends, often abbreviated as LoL, is a massively popular multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) video game developed and published by Riot Games. Released in 2009, the game has grown into a cultural phenomenon, boasting one of the largest player bases and most active esports scenes in the world.

In a standard match of League of Legends, two teams of five players compete against one another, with each player controlling a unique character known as a "champion." The primary objective is straightforward yet tactically demanding: destroy the opposing team's "Nexus," a structure located at the heart of their base, while defending your own.

sections.heading: The Core Gameplay Loop
paragraphs: Matches typically take place on a map called Summoner's Rift, which features three primary paths—referred to as lanes—connecting the two enemy bases. These lanes are guarded by powerful defensive towers and populated by waves of weaker, computer-controlled combatants called minions.

As players defeat minions, neutral monsters, and enemy champions, their characters earn gold and experience points. Gold is used to purchase items that enhance a champion's combat capabilities, while experience points allow them to level up and unlock powerful abilities. Teamwork, strategy, and rapid decision-making are essential, as players must constantly balance pushing lanes, securing map objectives, and supporting their teammates.

sections.heading: A Rich Roster of Champions
paragraphs: One of the defining features of League of Legends is its diverse and constantly expanding roster of champions. Each champion comes with a distinct visual design, a unique backstory rooted in the game's expansive fantasy universe (Runeterra), and an entirely different playstyle.

Champions generally fall into various role archetypes, such as tanks who absorb damage for the team, mages who wield powerful spellcasting abilities, marksmen who deal high physical damage from a distance, and support characters who heal and protect allies. This variety ensures that players can find a champion that suits their personal preferences, whether they prefer aggressive frontline combat or tactical support.

sections.heading: Cultural Impact and Esports
paragraphs: Beyond its millions of casual players, League of Legends helped shape the modern landscape of professional esports. Riot Games operates structured regional leagues across the globe, culminating in an annual World Championship event that draws massive global viewership.

The game's influence also extends well beyond traditional gaming. Riot Games has expanded the intellectual property into various forms of media, most notably through critically acclaimed animated series like Arcane, as well as virtual music groups, comic books, and extensive lore expansions that deepen the world of Runeterra.

faq.q: Is League of Legends free to play?
faq.a: Yes, League of Legends is free to download and play. The game's monetization relies primarily on optional cosmetic items, such as champion skins, which do not provide any competitive gameplay advantages.

faq.q: How many players are on each team?
faq.a: The standard game mode features two teams of five players each, requiring heavy coordination and communication to achieve victory.

faq.q: When was League of Legends released?
faq.a: League of Legends was officially released by Riot Games in October 2009 for Microsoft Windows, and later received support for macOS.
